- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.30) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below mean of recent 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots and forecasts too high — cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or 1.2x 30d moving average.
- If sentiment turns positive late in the window (e.g., last 3–5 days > 0.30), model underreacts — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% of recent 7-day mean.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for lagged rebound.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/– 0.30+), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
- If true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days), model is overconfident — reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 30d window.
- Sentiment > 0.30 in last 3 days + price drop > 3% → model often fails to anticipate reversal — add 1–2% upward bias to forecast to capture sentiment-driven bounce.
